## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review status: changes-requested
- Package members: design = docs/design/design/design.md; system = docs/design/system/system.md; workflow = docs/design/workflow/workflow.md. Exact identities are the stored subjects.
- Upstream review ID: proposal-review (approved; inspected unchanged proposal and its independent review).
- Review ID and round: design-review, initial assessment.
- Material findings: des-review-f1.
- Correction targets: design and workflow; authoring stage design, correction owner primary-agent.
- Recording status: recorded through targeted v2 review/finding batch.
- Open blockers: none requiring a missing owner decision or evidence acquisition; one actionable required correction prevents approval.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop; return the result to Route without selecting or mutating its next activity.
- Claim limitations: no Design approval, implementation authorization, verification, branch/PR readiness, coordinated adoption or publication. System has no separate component approval; judgment covers the complete three-member package.

## Assessment

The adopted Constitution model profile and current v2 record identify this exact model package; the fixed historical architecture/specification/ADR tuple is not mechanically reapplied to adopted models. The approved proposal explicitly selects reconciliation of separate authorship and fixed-package governance, while the draft correctly reserves activation for coordinated adoption. The reviewer did not edit any package member.

Behavior and realization are largely coherent: DES-SR-01–10 provide unified responsibility selection, behavior/feasibility reconciliation, technical concern coverage, stable embedded rationale, composition ownership, scoped consumer reconciliation and assessable outcomes. Material product-direction changes return to their owner. System's inventory distinguishes policy models from implementation/distribution boundaries and retained component owners. Its end-to-end counterexamples show why a local skill or model pass cannot establish a coherent routing/review/planning/install path. Test and Review and Closeout retain adequacy, applicability and assessment authority; Delivery retains checks, commands, fixtures and allocation. All eight model dimensions and requirement-linked integrated hazards are present.

The architecture-method R1–R124 map explicitly distinguishes preserved reasoning from intentionally replaced packaging and completed historical rollout. Inspected both method ADRs in full: the map preserves their main context, meaningful alternatives, no-temporary-truth rationale and changed consequences; exact historical bytes and approvals remain historical. The mixed-system map identifies selected sections and retains Level 2 and other responsibility details. Full migration and release/customer adoption are not inferred. Governance, source/public skill and relevant validation/package consumers are included for later concrete Delivery expansion; immutable historical releases/records are not bulk-edit targets. The remaining consolidation has maintainer direction ownership, Route assignment and a durable follow-up closeout obligation.

The chosen invocation withdrawal and operator-controlled cleanup are a bounded compatibility design. The existing init preflight and blocked-result mechanisms provide a credible implementation boundary; archive verification, no-write dry runs, unmanaged-file protection and existing workflow-to-route behavior retain their owners. This assessment is source inspection, not execution proof of the future guard. Portability uses compact common guidance plus explicit conditional methods and existing resource-integrity mechanisms; no new runtime schema or semantic dependency engine is selected.

A required migration-fidelity correction remains: the Workflow example contract is removed without a complete destination. Finding des-review-f1 gives the exact source obligations, missing replacement outcomes and safe repair. Broad claims of unchanged structural/example transfer and a section-level map cannot replace those omitted semantics. The correction is within approved direction, so the ordered judgment is changes-requested, not blocked or inconclusive.

## Finding des-review-f1

Severity: material. Scope: cross-artifact; members design and workflow; owning stage design. Locations: Design DES-SR-12, Model document and structural contract, Selected replacement map (Workflow model-convention row); Workflow Model-centered layout and examples and Model validation and proof mapping. The removed Workflow convention at the pre-authoring identity sha256:6b9fe7641466edfbb5bdc9b0e721f8085a3265f1572c05ece657dbeb00c49316 states: "The owning document indexes each example with its purpose, governing requirements, complete-artifact or excerpt scope, and any synthetic identities or starting assumptions." It further states: "JSON examples must parse without explanatory extra keys; complete records must conform to their selected schema when that schema is available. Before/after pairs must preserve the invariants they demonstrate." It requires independent review of affected examples alongside the owner and exact identities when relied upon. Those paragraphs are removed in the current Workflow diff and replaced by a Design ownership reference that expressly includes example indexing. Design DES-SR-12 preserves purpose, governing requirements, excerpt/complete scope, assumptions, on-demand loading and selector pairing; the full replacement document does not state JSON parse/schema conformance or before/after invariant preservation, and does not explicitly retain the parent index or the example-specific review handoff. The broad Workflow source-map row supplies no explicit retirement or other current owner for the omitted obligations. A complete JSON example carrying explanatory extra keys or a before/after pair violating its claimed invariant can therefore satisfy the enumerated replacement example rules while violating the source contract advertised as preserved. This is a contract-transfer gap under the accepted proposal's per-obligation reconciliation and DES-SR-11/13, not a request for exhaustive examples or Delivery test implementation.

Required outcome and safe resolution: Restore the retained example obligations under the Design owner and make their replacement mapping explicit: parent-model indexing; parseable JSON without explanatory extra keys; available-schema conformance for complete records; invariant preservation for before/after examples; and review of affected examples with exact identities when relied upon. Keep Workflow as a reference consumer and align the conditional model-authoring/review handoff and representative acceptance intent. If any obligation is intentionally replaced, state its precise alternative owner/outcome and justified disposition rather than claiming unchanged transfer. Safe resolution: the Design author makes the smallest destination/mapping correction, preserves old record identities and declares impact, then returns the exact affected package for independent reassessment. No product-direction decision or runtime-schema change is needed for the preservation correction.

## Evidence and limits

Read all three members completely; inspected their exact subjects, accepted proposal/review, Constitution, both selected method ADRs, source architecture-method clauses, selected mixed-system sections, current Workflow diff including displaced example paragraphs, Test/Review and Closeout requirements, architecture method resource and relevant skill/install consumer constraints. The pre-authoring Workflow identity is recorded in the authoring basis; the finding retains the substantive displaced text so resolution does not require old chat or Git. The current project map is not relied on: the accepted proposal identifies its older compact-record baseline as unsuitable for current ownership. Review uses direct subjects and named sources instead.

Independent command: python scripts/validate-boundary-first.py --path docs/design/design/design.md --path docs/design/system/system.md --path docs/design/workflow/workflow.md passed with structure-and-references-only. Author evidence reports prose/readability/link/enumeration checks against these same subjects; those remain bounded evidence, not semantic approval. No installer implementation tests, adapter generation, full CI or external runtime evaluation was run by this review. Record validation and git diff --check are checked after the save and reported in the handoff.

## Independence provenance

Separate delegated nonauthor agent task /root/independent_design_review, assigned after primary-agent completed Design, System and Workflow authorship under user direction. This reviewer authored or corrected none of those members and independently inspected their complete content, source displacement and governing basis. Separation is concrete contributor provenance, not the reviewer label or author self-checks.
